tracks.name: Part 0 · Biology from zero
tracks.blurb: No biology assumed. From atoms and cells to DNA, proteins, genetics, the immune system, lab techniques, cancer and how drugs work: everything the computational fields build on, explained simply, with interactive models and a little Python.

chapters.title: Life, scale and the cell
chapters.desc: What living things are made of, how big everything is, and a tour of the cell as a factory.

chapters.title: The chemistry of life
chapters.desc: Atoms, bonds, water, pH, energy, and the four families of molecules every cell is built from.

chapters.title: DNA and genomes
chapters.desc: The double helix, base pairing, chromosomes, how DNA is copied, and what a genome really contains.

chapters.title: From gene to protein
chapters.desc: Transcription, splicing, the genetic code and translation: how a DNA sequence becomes a working protein.

chapters.title: Proteins: shape is function
chapters.desc: Amino acids, folding, the four levels of structure, enzymes and how fast they work.

chapters.title: Gene regulation and epigenetics
chapters.desc: How a cell decides which genes to switch on: promoters, transcription factors, chromatin and cell identity.

chapters.title: The cell cycle, division and death
chapters.desc: Mitosis, meiosis, checkpoints, p53 and apoptosis: the machinery cancer breaks.

chapters.title: Genetics, mutation and evolution
chapters.desc: Inheritance, alleles, mutations, populations, natural selection and the tree of life.

chapters.title: Signalling and metabolism
chapters.desc: How cells sense and respond (receptors, kinase cascades) and how they make and use energy.

chapters.title: The immune system
chapters.desc: Innate and adaptive immunity, antibodies, T cells and the basis of vaccines and immunotherapy.

chapters.title: The lab toolkit
chapters.desc: PCR, gels, cloning, sequencing, CRISPR, microscopy and assays: where biological data comes from.

chapters.title: Cancer biology
chapters.desc: Oncogenes, tumour suppressors, the hallmarks of cancer, tumour evolution and how cancer is treated.

chapters.title: How drugs work
chapters.desc: Targets, binding, dose–response, potency and selectivity, ADME, and the drug-discovery pipeline.

tracks.name: Part 1 · Bioinformatics
tracks.blurb: Biological sequences as data: reading genomes, aligning sequences, building evolutionary trees, assembling genomes and finding variants, all from scratch on real data.

chapters.title: Sequences as data
chapters.desc: FASTA, GC content, k-mers, reading frames and gene finding in a real virus genome.

chapters.title: Sequence alignment from scratch
chapters.desc: Dynamic programming, Needleman–Wunsch and Smith–Waterman, substitution matrices, and how BLAST searches billions of letters.

chapters.title: Phylogenetics: trees of life
chapters.desc: Evolutionary distances, UPGMA and neighbour joining, and a tree of real viral genomes.

chapters.title: Genome assembly and read mapping
chapters.desc: Sequencing reads, quality scores, de Bruijn graph assembly and fast read mapping with k-mer indexes.

chapters.title: Variants and population genomics
chapters.desc: Calling variants, allele frequencies, Hardy–Weinberg, linkage and a genome-wide association study.

tracks.name: Part 2 · Omics and machine learning
tracks.blurb: Measuring thousands of genes at once and learning from it: RNA-seq, single-cell data, cancer classification and deep learning on DNA and proteins.

chapters.title: Transcriptomics and differential expression
chapters.desc: RNA-seq counts, normalisation, statistical testing with false-discovery control, on real tumour data.

chapters.title: Single-cell RNA-seq
chapters.desc: Quality control, PCA, neighbourhood graphs, clustering and cell-type annotation of 2,700 real blood cells.

chapters.title: Machine learning for cancer genomics
chapters.desc: Classifying tumours from gene expression honestly: high dimensions, feature selection, leakage and interpretation.

chapters.title: Deep learning on DNA
chapters.desc: One-hot sequences, convolutional networks that learn binding motifs, and how to read what they learned.

chapters.title: Protein machine learning and AlphaFold
chapters.desc: Sequence embeddings, coevolution, contact prediction and how AlphaFold and protein language models work.

tracks.name: Part 3 · Structure, chemistry and drug discovery
tracks.blurb: Molecules in 3D, physics-based simulation and the computational side of finding new medicines.

chapters.title: Protein structure
chapters.desc: PDB files, coordinates, contacts, RMSD and superposition, binding pockets and AlphaFold confidence.

chapters.title: Molecular dynamics from scratch
chapters.desc: Force fields, Verlet integration, temperature, and a toy protein that folds on a lattice.

chapters.title: Cheminformatics
chapters.desc: Molecules as graphs: SMILES, descriptors, fingerprints, drug-likeness and similarity search with RDKit.

chapters.title: QSAR and virtual screening
chapters.desc: Predicting activity against a cancer target from real ChEMBL data, with honest scaffold splits.

chapters.title: Docking and binding
chapters.desc: Scoring functions, a docking search from scratch, and what binding free energy means.

chapters.title: Pharmacokinetics and dosing
chapters.desc: Compartment models, half-life, dosing regimens and dose–response, as differential equations.

tracks.name: Part 4 · Systems biology and simulation
tracks.blurb: Cells and tissues as dynamical systems: gene circuits, noise, and the evolution of tumours, simulated.

chapters.title: Gene circuits as dynamical systems
chapters.desc: Differential equations for gene expression: switches, oscillators and feedback.

chapters.title: Noise and stochastic simulation
chapters.desc: Why identical cells differ: the Gillespie algorithm and bursting gene expression.

chapters.title: Tumour growth and cancer evolution
chapters.desc: Growth laws, agent-based tumours, clonal evolution and how drug resistance emerges.

tracks.name: Part 5 · Cancer research and capstones
tracks.blurb: Real cancer genomics and clinical data, then end-to-end projects that use the whole course.

chapters.title: Cancer genomics and mutational signatures
chapters.desc: Driver genes, mutation spectra and signature extraction with non-negative matrix factorisation.

chapters.title: Survival analysis
chapters.desc: Kaplan–Meier curves, log-rank tests and Cox models on real patient cohorts.

chapters.title: Capstone: a drug-discovery campaign
chapters.desc: From a cancer target to ranked candidate molecules: data, models, screening, filtering and a report.

chapters.title: Capstone: a precision-oncology analysis
chapters.desc: From a tumour cohort's mutations and expression to subtypes, biomarkers and outcomes.
